rows.title: PureTech 1.2 Wet Timing Belt Delamination
rows.howToFix: If an oil-pressure warning appears, stop the engine as soon as it is safe and do not continue driving until the lubrication system is checked. Identify engine and production date by VIN, inspect belt condition using the current Peugeot procedure, and when degradation is confirmed follow engine-specific instructions for the timing-belt system, oil pickup/lubrication circuit, oil and filter. Check Peugeot support eligibility and the service schedule. Do not buy a timing-belt kit from this page; production date, engine, diagnosis and VIN fitment must be established first.

rows.title: e-2008 Range Below Advertised
rows.howToFix: Perform a battery recalibration by fully charging then fully depleting the battery twice. Use eco mode and pre-condition while plugged in. A software update may improve BMS estimation accuracy.

rows.title: Fuel Gauge Sender Unit Failure
rows.howToFix: Access the sender through the hatch under the rear seat cushion, clean and re-tension the connector terminals and inspect the wiring; if the float or resistive track is worn, replace the sender (or combined pump/sender) unit. No tank removal is required.

rows.title: Ignition Coil Pack Failure (Petrol TU Engines)
rows.howToFix: Replace the coil pack — OEM-quality (Sagem/Valeo/Bosch) units are strongly recommended over cheap aftermarket packs — along with spark plugs if worn. The job is a straightforward DIY or sub-one-hour shop task on these engines.

rows.title: Rear Axle Torsion Beam Trailing Arm Bearing Wear
rows.howToFix: If caught early, fit a trailing arm bearing and shaft repair kit; once the axle tube bearing surfaces are scored, the accepted fix is a fully reconditioned exchange rear axle from a specialist, followed by rear geometry/ride-height check. Repairing a seized, rusted original axle DIY is generally considered impractical.

rows.title: Power Steering Pump Leak
rows.howToFix: Replace the power steering pump seals or the complete pump assembly. Flush and refill the power steering fluid system.

rows.title: Window Regulator Failure
rows.howToFix: Replace the window regulator assembly. Upgraded aftermarket units with reinforced cables are available and recommended over OEM replacements.

rows.title: BSI (Built-in Systems Interface) Body Control Unit Faults
rows.howToFix: First attempt the documented BSI reset (controlled battery disconnect/reboot sequence); persistent faults require repair of the unit's solder joints by a specialist or a replacement BSI that must be coded/cloned to the car. Address water ingress at the bonnet vent and plenum drains to prevent recurrence.
rows.dispositionReason: The remedy is a service, tool, consumable, or fluid procedure rather than a repair part.

rows.title: COM2000 Indicator/Wiper Stalk Unit Failure
rows.howToFix: Replace the COM2000 unit (roughly £130-£180 for the part depending on trim, plus fitting behind the steering wheel); confident DIYers sometimes succeed in cleaning and re-greasing the internal contacts, but unit replacement is the accepted lasting fix.
rows.dispositionReason: No positive owner-buyable repair prescription was found.

rows.title: Gearbox Input Shaft Bearing Noise
rows.howToFix: Replace the input shaft bearing. This requires gearbox removal but is significantly cheaper than a full gearbox replacement if caught early.
rows.dispositionReason: The solution prescribes an owner-buyable component or existing commerce requires re-review.

rows.title: Timing Chain Tensioner Failure
rows.howToFix: Replace the timing chain, tensioner, and guides with the updated revision parts. Ensure correct oil specification (0W-30) is used to maintain hydraulic tensioner pressure.
rows.dispositionReason: The solution prescribes an owner-buyable component or existing commerce requires re-review.

rows.title: Turbocharger Oil Leak
rows.howToFix: Replace the turbo oil feed and return lines with updated gaskets. If bearings are worn, a turbo rebuild or replacement is necessary. Use manufacturer-recommended oil change intervals.
rows.dispositionReason: The solution prescribes an owner-buyable component or existing commerce requires re-review.

rows.title: AdBlue/SCR System Failure on BlueHDi Diesels — Urea Fault With Start-Prevention Countdown

Independent specialists and aftermarket repair kits can substantially undercut dealer pricing; do not ignore the countdown, as the car will refuse to restart at zero.

Persistent faults are fixed by specialist BSI board repair (about $100–200) or a replacement unit coded to the car; many faults after battery changes clear with a dealer diagnostic reset.

rows.howToFix: The accepted fix in the owner community is to remove the hydraulic self-levelling unit entirely and convert to conventional rear shock absorbers (the dampers from the 1.6 model are a direct fit), a roughly half-hour job that saves several hundred pounds over replacing the hydraulic system. Genuine HV pack failures are addressed with refurbished or repaired battery packs from hybrid specialists at a fraction of the new-unit price.

Outside the recall, replace the wet belt early (around 6 years/60k miles rather than the original 10-year schedule) and use only the specified PSA B71 2010 0W-30 oil with shortened oil-change intervals.

rows.howToFix: First attempt a soft reset by holding the phone/source button for around 10 seconds; the lasting fix is a dealer (or USB self-service via Peugeot Update) NAC firmware update per the TSB. rows.title: DPF Regeneration Failure

rows.title: EGR Valve Failure
rows.howToFix: Clean or replace the EGR valve. Install an EGR cooler bypass blanking kit if permitted in your region. Update the ECU software to revised EGR control maps.

rows.title: 1.6 HDi (DV6) Turbocharger Failure from Oil Starvation and Sludge
rows.howToFix: Replace the turbocharger together with new oil feed and return pipes and the banjo-bolt filter, drop and clean the sump and oil pickup, and flush the engine — about $1,200-2,600 all-in at an independent shop. Prevent recurrence with strictly shortened oil-change intervals using the correct low-SAPS oil and prompt attention to injector seal leaks.

rows.title: 1.6 THP Intake Valve Carbon Buildup (Direct Injection)

Quality fuel and regular oil changes slow, but do not prevent, re-accumulation.

rows.title: Electric Parking Brake (EPB) Faults — Caliper Motor, Switch and Wiring

After any rear brake work, the actuators must be retracted and recalibrated electronically to avoid inducing the fault.
